scientific_scope_status: In the declared two-port finite-band Fano model, a shared positive rank-one auxiliary residue can supply cross-port response that scalar side modes cannot. Given exact kernel derivatives and positive-control sign checks, the written controls cancel both selected detuning and unwanted-port coefficients through second order at one energy. Positive scalar-pole moments separately constrain allowable poles and third derivatives; that restricted class does not include the matrix residue. A strict zero-energy Schur form margin plus charge-compatible memory gives an all-sector saturation implication, not a continuum spectral gap or a single-impurity capacity-two theorem. Unequal port delays change the spectral measure; a constant counterterm cannot restore the entire old off-axis self-energy, though local retuning remains possible.
